```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(gt)
```


## Exercise 1: Using functions
```{r}
# whole number
round(3.14159)

# two digits after decimal point
round(3.14159, digits = 2)
```

## Exercise 2: Argument order
```{r}
# specified by order
print(rep(5, 7))

# using keywords
print(rep(x = 5, times = 7))
```

## Exercise 3: Character, numerical and logical variables
Character
```{r}
my_char <- "this is a character variable"
print(class(my_char))
```
Numerical
```{r}
my_num <- 1
print(class(my_num))
```
Logical
```{r}
my_logic <- TRUE
print(class(my_logic))
```

## Exercise 4: Using variables of different types
```{r}
cell_id_1 <- "CX1"
cell_id_2 <- "CX2"
treated_1 <- TRUE
treated_2 <- FALSE
num_cells_before_1 <- 5415
num_cells_before_2 <- 8123
num_cells_after_1 <- 1432
num_cells_after_2 <- 7543
```

## Bonus Exercise
```{r}
print(TRUE + TRUE)
print(TRUE + FALSE)
print(5 + TRUE)
```
TRUE is converted to 1.
FALSE is converted to 0.

```{r}
x <- NA
print(x == NA)
print(is.na(x))
```
NA refers to an unknown / missing value, so == NA is invalid. Use is.na to check.

```{r}
x <- 0 / 0
print(x)
print(is.na(x))
print(is.nan(x))
```
NaN is a special kind of missing value (Not a Number). (A NaN value is always NA but an NA value is not always NaN?)

```{r}
print(round(2.5))
print(round(3.5))
```
R uses "round to even" for numbers exactly halfway between 2 values to reduce bias.

```{r}
print(1/0)
print(-1/0)
```
Inf and -Inf are positive infinity and negative infinity. NULL represents a value that doesn't exist.

# Exercise 5: Vectors
```{r}
cell_id <- c(cell_id_1, cell_id_2)
treated <- c(treated_1, treated_2)
num_cells_before <- c(num_cells_before_1, num_cells_before_2)
num_cells_after <- c(num_cells_after_1, num_cells_after_2)
```

# Exercise 6: Indexing
```{r}
all_my_pets <- c("dog", "horse", "guinea pig", "chicken", "cat")
my_pet <- all_my_pets[4]
print(my_pet)
```

# Bonus Exercise
```{r}
x <- c(2, -4, 6, -2)
# apply functions to all values of vectors like this:
x * 2
x > 5
sum(x)
abs(x)
```

# Exercise 7: Creating a data frame
```{r}
# using values
my_data_frame <- tibble(
  cell_ID = c(cell_id_1, cell_id_2),
  treated = c(treated_1, treated_2),
  num_cells_before = c(num_cells_before_1, num_cells_before_2),
  num_cells_after = c(num_cells_after_1, num_cells_after_2)
)

gt(my_data_frame)
```

```{r}
# using vectors
my_data_frame <- tibble(
  cell_ID = cell_id,
  treated = treated,
  num_cells_before = num_cells_before,
  num_cells_after = num_cells_after_1, num_cells_after_2
)

gt(my_data_frame)
```
